subject: Operations
title: The Reshoring Movement
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Reshoring Movement.

hook.text: After decades of offshoring, firms bring factories home. The cheap-labor advantage is shrinking. Reshoring is rising.

buildup.text: Reshoring means moving operations back to the home country after previously offshoring them.

discovery.text: Drivers: rising overseas wages, automation cutting domestic labor costs, supply chain risk, and demand for local goods.

twist.text: Reshoring isn't free—rebuilding domestic supply bases takes years and the skilled workforce may no longer exist.

climax.text: The US CHIPS Act offers $52 billion to reshore semiconductor manufacturing. Government policy is accelerating the trend.

punchline.text: Reshoring is strategic, not nostalgic. The math is changing.

quiz.question: What is driving the reshoring movement?
options: Rising overseas wages and supply chain risk
